root_cause: JsonTree concatenates object keys into dotted text; Network rowsFromBody and Framework next_data split that text on dots. A literal key containing a dot becomes indistinguishable from two nested keys.

persisted_contract_found.current: Saved pattern config stores key_path as a JSON string. The Framework and Network schemas accept strings, both live runners consume strings, and existing recipes use dotted strings. SaveAsPattern passes config to savePattern without rewriting the key path.
persisted_contract_found.compatibility_constraint: A valid old key_path such as ["literal"] can name an actual literal key. Interpreting bracket syntax inside every old string would redirect it to the different key literal. A versioned string without an independent format marker still collides with possible existing string values.

candidate.representation: key_path is string | string[]. Existing strings retain the exact dotted split behavior. New JsonTree selections are arrays of literal object-key segments, serialized directly in the same JSON config field. The array type is the unambiguous structural discriminator; no parser or duplicate source of truth is introduced.
candidate.scope: JsonTree emits segments; Network preview and saved replay traverse them; Framework preview and saved replay traverse them inside the injected runner; the Zod mode schemas accept both persisted shapes. Formatting is only for display and is never parsed for extraction.
candidate.reason_against_versioned_string: Any reserved string prefix can already be a saved dotted path or literal object key, so the prefix alone cannot preserve all existing valid recipes. A separate version marker would be a second persisted field that must stay synchronized. JSON array versus string gives the discriminator in the path value itself.

source_evidence.census: JsonTree has two production callers: NetworkTab and FrameworkTab. The only extraction consumers of key_path are rowsFromBody, runNetworkCapturePattern, and next_data.runInPage; the latter runs through both runMode and runPattern. Existing recipe literals remain strings.
